identity.title: ALMACAL V: absorption-selected galaxies with evidence for excited ISMs

question.value: What are the CO excitation (CO SLED) and molecular gas conditions of absorption-selected galaxies, and are Galactic CO line ratios and alpha_CO applicable?

evidence.quote: We infer that the CO line ratios and the $\alpha_{\rm CO}$ conversion factor differ from the Galactic values.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00989.S, #2016.1.01435.S, #2015.1.01084.S
We cannot use the Band 6 observations to measure the continuum flux of J0238A and J0238A1, because of strong residuals from the quasar continuum. In Band 7 we do not see any residuals

what.value: J0423B properties, absorber gas properties, impact parameters

what.value: Gas properties of absorbers and host galaxies

evidence.quote: taken from (cite: Klitsch2018; Rao2006; Junkkarinen2004; Burbidge1996)

what.value: CO line flux to L'_line conversion

evidence.quote: We convert the CO line flux to $L'_{\rm line}$ following the description from (cite: Solomon1992).
This is converted to the SFR using the (cite: Kennicutt1998) relation.

method.value: Cross-correlate absorber positions with calibrators and match CO frequency coverage with absorber redshift

evidence.quote: Cross-correlating the sky positions of known absorbers detected at optical and UV wavelengths with the 749 calibrators in our ALMACAL catalogue leads to 109 positional matches.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract CO spectra and line fluxes

method.value: Moment maps integrated over w20; spectra from aperture enclosing 3 sigma contours; line flux integrated over w20

evidence.quote: The spectra are measured using an aperture that encompasses the $3\sigma$ contours in the moment map. The line flux is determined by integrating over $w_{20}$.

method.value: Scale starburst templates to 870 um flux, integrate 8-1000 um to get L_FIR, convert to SFR

evidence.quote: The fitted spectrum is then integrated in the wavelength range from $8$ - $1000 \:\mu \text{m}$ to obtain the total far-infrared luminosity $L_{\rm FIR}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Construct CO SLEDs and compute molecular gas masses

method.value: Normalize SLED to CO(2-1); convert CO(2-1) to CO(1-0) with r21 = 0.9 and derive masses in M_sun/alpha_CO

evidence.quote: We convert the line luminosities using the median conversion factor $r_{21} = L'_{\rm CO(2-1)}/L'_{\rm CO(1-0)} = 0.9$ for LIRGs (cite: Papadopoulos2012a).

assumptions.value: LIRG-like r21 = 0.9; masses expressed in units of M_sun/alpha_CO

evidence.quote: Instead, we argue that for the absorption-selected galaxies studied here, LIRG-like conversion factors are more appropriate.

validation.value: Compared with Milky Way, BzK, LIRG SLEDs and L'CO-LFIR relation

evidence.quote: Comparing the L$'_{\rm CO}$–L$_{{\rm FIR}}$ relation we find that J0423B is consistent with local LIRGs

analysis_steps.goal: Test correlations of L_CO with impact parameter and N(HI)

method.value: Pearson correlation coefficient with this sample and Kanekar2018

evidence.quote: Using the Pearson correlation coefficient we find a correlation between $L_{\rm CO}$ and the impact parameter with a p-value of 0.01
we exclude it from the analysis resulting in p-values of 0.1 and 0.01

correlation between $L_{\rm CO}$ and the impact parameter with a p-value of 0.01

findings_qualitative.value: CO SLEDs of J0238A and A1 are more excited than normal star-forming galaxies; J0423B only slightly steeper than the Milky Way

evidence.quote: The CO SLEDs of J0238A and J0238A1 are clearly distinct from the CO SLED of the Milky Way or $BzK$ galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Absorption-selected galaxies have CO excitation like normal star-forming galaxies
claims.experiment: Compare CO SLEDs normalized to CO(2-1) with Milky Way and BzK galaxies
claims.result: J0238A and A1 have more excited SLEDs; J0423B only slightly steeper than the Milky Way
claims.finding: Galactic line ratios and alpha_CO may not apply to some absorption-selected galaxies

evidence.quote: Our findings suggest that at least a fraction of absorption selected systems shows ISM conditions deviating from those of normal star-forming galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: L_CO correlates with impact parameter and N(HI)
claims.finding: Only the impact-parameter correlation is rejected as null at 0.05 level; small sample

evidence.quote: However, the results are based on a small dataset and more data is needed to further investigate these correlations.

limitations_admitted.value: CO(1-0) not observed so SLEDs normalized to CO(2-1); small sample

evidence.quote: the CO(1–0) emission line was not observed towards the absorption-selected galaxies

referee_caveats_inferred: Only three galaxies; statistical correlations weak
r21 and alpha_CO assumed from LIRGs without independent constraint
Reduction details deferred to other papers
